Thus the correct reading in M: tragically ὁπλοκτύπος τί χρίμπτεται [the clash of arms somehow approaches], as two or more say in the Preface of the fifth Leipzig edition p. XXXB and in Philologus vol. 16 p. 293. 294. In most copies it is ὠτὶ (or ὠσί) χρίμπτεται [approaches the ears], which some corrector's invention followed, who explains: ποιεῖ προσπελάζειν τὸν ἦχον τοῖς ὠσίν [makes the sound approach the ears].

Ὦ βροτῶν πάντων ὑπερσχὼν ὄλβον εὐτυχεῖ [O you who surpass all mortals in happiness of wealth]
Οἴκων γὰρ εὐθυδίκων καλλίπαις [for of houses justly governed, fair of children]
Οὑμὸς δὲ πότμος οὐρανῷ κυρῶν [But my fate, reaching to heaven]
Thus Porson corrects what is read in Plutarch Mor. p. 603: θυμός δέ ποθ᾽ ἁμός [but my spirit at some time].
